name_note: GTDB R232 g__Ruminococcus is narrower than the classical genus Ruminococcus: Ruminococcus bromii and Ruminococcus gnavus are placed in other GTDB genera, while this genus keeps Ruminococcus flavefaciens and related uncultured human and rumen Ruminococcus species.

sentences.text: Ruminococcus flavefaciens is described as one of the three predominant cellulolytic bacterial species found in the rumen.
Ruminococcus flavefaciens is a major plant cell wall degrading bacterium that assembles its catalytic apparatus into a large multienzyme complex, the cellulosome.

High throughput screening of protein modules of unknown function identified six previously unidentified carbohydrate binding module families in R. flavefaciens targeting b-glucans, b-mannans and the pectic polysaccharide homogalacturonan.

A study identified ruminococcal species in the gut microbiota of human populations that assemble functional cellulosome structures, and reported them abundant among hunter-gatherers and rural populations but rare in industrialized societies.
A study in mice reported that supplementation with R. flavefaciens diminished a duloxetine-induced decrease in depressive-like behaviour.
